subject: math

objective.text: Make a ten to add. Take from a ten to subtract. Use it with numbers to 100.

source_ref.section: Lesson objectives of L1 to L8 (make ten, add to ten, like units, take from ten)

explanations.title: L1 Ten-frame: 9 and 1 make 10
explanations.text: A ten-frame has 10 spots. Here 9 spots are full. Only 1 spot is empty. So 9 plus 1 equals 10. Also, 10 minus 1 equals 9. And 10 minus 9 equals 1.

source_ref.section: L1 Fluency: Ten-Frame Flash

explanations.title: L1 Number bond to 10
explanations.text: A number bond shows a total and two parts. The total is the big number. Here the total is 10. If one part is 5, the other part is 5. So 5 plus 5 equals 10.

source_ref.section: L1 Fluency: Pairs to Ten with Number Bonds

explanations.title: L1 Say Ten way
explanations.text: Some people say numbers the Say Ten way. You say the ten first, then the ones. 13 is said ten 3. Ten 3 means 10 plus 3. So 10 plus 3 equals 13.

source_ref.section: L1 Fluency: Happy Counting the Say Ten Way

explanations.title: L1 Add a ten and some ones
explanations.text: When you add 10 and some ones, the answer has a ten and those ones. Look at ten 5. It means 10 plus 5. So 10 plus 5 equals 15.

source_ref.section: L1 Fluency: Say Ten as Ten Plus Facts

explanations.title: L2 Value of tens and ones
explanations.text: A quick ten is a stick of 10. Count the tens first. Then count the ones. 2 tens and 2 ones make 22. 20 plus 2 equals 22.

source_ref.section: L2 Fluency: The Value of Tens and Ones

explanations.title: L2 Make the next ten
explanations.text: 8 needs 2 to make the next ten. 28 needs 2 to make 30. 58 needs 2 to make 60. The ones tell you how many.

source_ref.section: L2 Fluency: Make the Next Ten (8, 28, 58: S: 2)

explanations.title: L2 A ten fact helps with other tens
explanations.text: Knowing 10 plus 3 helps with 50 plus 3. Both add 3 ones. 10 plus 3 equals 13. So 50 plus 3 equals 53.

source_ref.section: L2 Student Debrief (how does knowing 10 + 3 help us with 50 + 3)

explanations.title: L3 Add and subtract ones
explanations.text: Use an easier fact. 5 plus 2 equals 7. So 45 plus 2 equals 47. Only the ones change. The tens stay the same.

source_ref.section: L3 Concept Development Part 1

explanations.title: L3 Add and subtract tens
explanations.text: Add tens to tens. 5 tens plus 2 tens equals 7 tens. So 50 plus 20 equals 70. And 51 plus 20 equals 71.

source_ref.section: L3 Concept Development Part 2

explanations.title: L4 Make a ten to add
explanations.text: To add 9 plus 4, make a ten first. Break 4 into 1 and 3. 9 plus 1 equals 10. Then 10 plus 3 equals 13.

source_ref.section: L4 Concept Development Part 1

explanations.title: L4 Patterns for 9 and 8
explanations.text: When you add 9, you take 1 out of the other number. When you add 8, you take 2 out.

source_ref.section: L4 Concept Development Part 2

explanations.title: L5 Make a ten within 100
explanations.text: To add 39 plus 4, break 4 into 1 and 3. 39 plus 1 equals 40. Then 40 plus 3 equals 43.

source_ref.section: L5 Concept Development

explanations.title: L6 Take from a ten (multiples of ten)
explanations.text: To take 9 from 20, break 20 into 10 and 10. 10 minus 9 equals 1. Then 10 plus 1 equals 11.

source_ref.section: L6 Concept Development Part 1

explanations.title: L7 Take from a ten (teen numbers)
explanations.text: To take 9 from 12, break 12 into 2 and 10. 10 minus 9 equals 1. Then 1 plus 2 equals 3.

source_ref.section: L7 Concept Development Part 1

explanations.title: L8 Take from the ones or from a ten
explanations.text: Look at the ones. If you have enough ones, take from the ones. If not, take from a ten.

source_ref.section: L8 Fluency: Take from a Ten or Take from the Ones

explanations.title: L8 Take from a ten within 100
explanations.text: To take 8 from 23, break 23 into 13 and 10. 10 minus 8 equals 2. Then 13 plus 2 equals 15.

source_ref.section: L8 Concept Development

misconceptions.label: Mixing up fourteen and forty
misconceptions.description: The English word fourteen puts the ones before the ten, so a child can confuse a teen number with a tens number such as forty.
detection_signals: Child says 'forty' or answers 40 when fourteen (or 10 plus 4) is expected.
Child answers a tens number such as 40 for a teen-number sum.
misconceptions.response_text: Careful, fourteen is not forty. Fourteen is said ten 4. It means 10 plus 4.

source_ref.section: L1 Fluency: Happy Counting the Say Ten Way (note: fourteen is easily confused with forty)

misconceptions.label: Taking from the ten and forgetting the extra ones
misconceptions.description: In 12 minus 9, the child takes 9 from the ten and says what is left of the ten. The 2 extra ones are forgotten.
detection_signals: Answer equals 10 minus the number taken (for example 1 for 12 minus 9).
Child says the answer to the take-from-ten step and stops.
misconceptions.response_text: You took 9 from the ten. Do not forget the extra ones. Add them to what is left.

review_flags.item: whole card (8 lessons in one card)
review_flags.issue: By request this ONE card covers all 8 lessons of Module 1 (zip). The prompt rules say one lesson per card, so this deviates: one objective for the whole module, more than 5 explanations, and ids carry the lesson number (for example q_pr_l4_1). Lesson is also named in every source_ref.section. The Planner may need lesson-level cards. Decide with the team.

The source is 8 markdown files with no printed page numbers, no images and no 'This file derived from' footer. Every page is 'n/a' with a section name. source_version is 'not_stated_in_file' and source_refs holds one item for the whole zip. Fill both in from the original PDFs.

The worksheets have no printed titles in these files. They were named by order after the Exit Ticket instructions: Lessons 1 to 3 start with Sprint A and Sprint B. Lessons 3 to 8 then show Problem Set, Exit Ticket, Homework. Lessons 1 and 2 show Exit Ticket, Homework. A person must confirm this against the PDFs. Section names that say Problem Set, Exit Ticket or Homework depend on it.

review_flags.item: picture-only and blank items not used
review_flags.issue: These items are pictures or have no numbers in the text, so no question was made: L1 and L2 number bonds to complete or draw (Exit Ticket, Homework), L2 Exit Ticket (Solve 1 and 2 are blank), L2 Number Bond Dash, L4 Homework 9 (match), L5 Exit Ticket (Maria's work), L6 Exit Ticket 2 (fill in the number bond), L6 Homework 1 (take out ten for 40 to 80), L7 and L8 Homework 'Take out ten' bonds. A person must read the PDF images.
All 5 assets (a_ten_frame, a_number_bond, a_say_ten_rekenrek, a_quick_ten_drawing, a_five_group_column) are not_available. Questions and explanations that use them cannot launch until they exist.
The source is a teacher script for a class with a Rekenrek, cards and partners. All child text was rewritten for a screen. Needs age-appropriate wording review.

ext_g1_add_subtract_within_10, ext_k_say_ten_counting and ext_g1_place_value_tens_ones are external prerequisite cards that do not exist yet. The source names Grade 1 and Kindergarten work as earlier learning but does not teach it.

The source prints no answers for Sprints, Exit Tickets, Homework or Problem Sets, and none for most Fluency and word-problem items. Every such key is derived. Each was solved by code from the printed item, then checked against the lesson text.

L1 Sprint A: items 3, 22, 26, 28, 30 used. Left out: 16 (3 + 10), 27 (8 + ? = 18), 29 (19 = ? + 10), which repeat a pattern already covered. L2 Sprint A: items 4, 7, 16, 25, 28, 30 used. Left out: 27 and 29, same patterns. L3 Sprint A: items 1, 22, 25, 26, 27, 29 used. Sprint B of every lesson repeats the same patterns, so no Sprint B items were added.

review_flags.item: Problem Set, Exit Ticket and Homework items left out
review_flags.issue: Not every printed item became a question. Items left out repeat a pattern already covered in the same lesson (for example L8 Problem Set 1 other rows, L5 Problem Set 1 other rows, L6 Problem Set 1 other rows). Only one or two items per pattern were used. If the team wants all items, add them from the PDFs.

Open debrief questions were made only where the source asks a clear reflection question. The favorite-fact, hope-to-improve and teach-someone-else prompts, and the repeated name-the-lesson prompt (kept for L1 and L8 only), were left out. The source gives no answers for any debrief prompt, so all 12 rubrics are open and derived.

Only 2 are stated in the source: fourteen mixed up with forty (mis_teen_forty), and forgetting the extra ones after taking from the ten (mis_forgot_ones, from the pretend-fingers moment in L7). Proposals, not added: mixing up the ones in 2 ones and 2 tens (L3); answering with the total instead of the missing part (L1, L4); adding the digits of a tens-and-ones number (L2 q_pk_l2_1, q_pk_l2_2).

The prompt asks for 2 to 5 explanations. This module card has 15 (one or two per lesson) because it covers 8 lessons. Lessons 2, 5, 6, 7 and 8 have a single approach each, so the Planner has little real choice there.
These 6 hints are origin 'generated' (not in the source). The other 16 hints are adapted from teacher moves and notes. Hint coverage is thin. Levels and wording need review.
Single-number answers have no real partial outcome. The script must map a null partial to the same path as incorrect, or the shared schema must allow null.
